purpose: One-shot constructive image-design exploration, separate from bounded font council.
explicitly_adopted_reference_setup: Fresh reference.tex borrows fontspec/unicode-math rendering setup from active tools/greek_proofs.py; existing campaign files read-only.
chosen_design_reference: František Štorm, inspiration only, not an authorship claim
tool_mode: built-in image_gen; no CLI fallback authorized
generation_mode: One built-in image_gen call with exact current-design PNG reference; no CLI, retries, image post-processing or upscaling.
useful_ideas: Greek nu acquires a broader, more flowing right arm/entry relationship in the large row, with a clearer pointed-versus-rounded nu/upsilon contrast.
Large beta, theta, phi and omega suggest more expansive white and rounded calligraphic turns against firm vertical strokes.
Variant/style rows encourage testing a coherent family gesture rather than only local geometric fixes.
limitations: Output is1055x1491 pixels, substantially below the4961x7016 reference; it is not a600dpi deliverable. The original was saved without artificial upscaling.
This is a raster visual idea, not a font, compiled outlines, exact metrics, kerning, MATH data or validated glyph coverage.
The model largely retained the reference sheet structure; substantial originality or a faithful match to any actual Storm typeface is not established.
The generated heat-kernel integral visibly loses the lower integration limit, and small script identities/indices are altered or indistinct.
Variant rows are redundant, with inconsistent labelling and potentially weakened kappa/epsilon distinctions. The large v/nu/upsilon row has no individual labels and changes the Latin-v appearance.
Generated prose/math must not be used as ground-truth typography or exact mathematical copy; all potential design ideas require deliberate reconstruction and normal proofing.
